rows.title: Using your phone to pay is convenient, but it can also mean you spend more
rows.standfirst: Consumers tend to spend about 10% more when they adopt mobile contactless payment methods, according to research from Assistant Professor Yuqian Xu at UNC-Chapel Hill.

rows.title: Some Walmart shoppers could get up to $500 in cash from a class-action settlement
rows.standfirst: Customers who bought certain grocery products at Walmart stores nationwide between October 2018 and January 2024 have until early June to file for payments, whether or not they kept their receipts.

rows.title: Do I need a four-year degree?
rows.standfirst: The U.S. labor market continues its hot streak, adding 303,000 jobs last month — more than expected. Many of these jobs will require a four-year degree despite a push among some employers to eliminate these requirements. On today's show, we look at the state of the job market for people without a four-year college degree.

rows.title: Japan had a vibrant economy. Then it fell into a slump for 30 years.
rows.standfirst: Last month, Japan's central bank raised interest rates for the first time in 17 years. That is a really big deal, because it means that one of the spookiest stories in modern economics might finally have an ending.

rows.title: 99 Cents stores to close down all 371 locations
rows.standfirst: The discount chain is winding down operations at its stores across California, Texas, Arizona and Nevada, as dollar stores nationwide buckle under inflation, shoplifting and other factors.

rows.title: Construction boom helps fuel job gains in March
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 303,000 jobs last month, and the unemployment rate dipped to 3.8%. Construction companies added 39,000 jobs, despite high interest rates.

rows.title: Seeking to defy history, the UAW is coming closer to unionizing in the South
rows.standfirst: Autoworkers at Volkswagen's plant in Chattanooga, Tenn., will vote in mid-April on whether to join the United Auto Workers union. Mercedes workers in Tuscaloosa County, Ala., will soon follow.

rows.title: Black market cannabis thrives in California despite legalization
rows.standfirst: Marijuana legalization was expected to bring the industry out of the shadows. But in some states, the black market is alive and well.

rows.title: McDonald's says it is buying back all of its franchises in Israel
rows.standfirst: Alonyal Limited owns 225 McDonald's locations. McDonald's has recently faced boycotts after its Israel branch donated meals to the Israeli military.

rows.title: How the 'shadow fleet' helps Russia skirt sanctions
rows.standfirst: "Shadow fleet" refers to the collective of ships used by countries that have sanctions against them, like Russia, to transport commodities around the world. These ships pose threats to global and environmental security because they skirt international maritime law. So what can be done about them?

rows.title: Amazon is cutting hundreds of jobs in its cloud computing unit AWS
rows.standfirst: The AWS layoffs follow other layoffs that happened at Amazon and its subsidiaries this year, including at Prime Video, the MGM Studios unit and Twitch, the social media platform owned by Amazon.

rows.title: The real estate industry on trial
rows.standfirst: In 2019, Mike Ketchmark got a call. Mike is a lawyer in Kansas City, Missouri, and his friend, Brandon Boulware, another lawyer, was calling about a case he wanted Mike to get involved with. Mike was an unusual choice - he's a personal injury lawyer, and this was going to be an antitrust case.

rows.title: No more 'just walk out' at Amazon grocery stores. The new bet is smart shopping carts
rows.standfirst: The retailer banked big on the cashier-less tech. It's now out at Amazon Fresh stores in the U.S. But Amazon's grocery ambitions are only shapeshifting.

rows.title: Taiwan earthquake briefly halts chip factories that power the global economy
rows.standfirst: The Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., which makes more than 90% of world's most advanced chips, also halted production, but it plans to resume chipmaking overnight.

rows.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese's LSU-Iowa rematch nets a record audience for ESPN
rows.standfirst: Iowa and LSU drew the second-largest audience for any basketball game on ESPN since 2012, the network said. Reese said Wednesday that like Clark, she will leave college for the pros.

rows.title: Google blocks California news in response to bill that would force tech giant to pay
rows.standfirst: The company on Friday said it has started blocking California-based news outlets to protest a pending bill that supporters say would extend a lifeline to the ailing news industry.

rows.title: TikTok is filled with tax advice. Is any of it worth listening to?
rows.standfirst: TikTok, and other apps like it, are filled with financial advice. Some of it is reliable, some... less so.

rows.title: What Subway's foot-long cookie says about inflation
rows.standfirst: In this edition of Indicators of the Week: the new incentive for speed in cash prizes for Olympic track and field, growing iPhone assembly in India and the curious inflation puzzle of the foot-long cookies at Subway.

rows.title: The Forever Stamp just went up in price. How does the U.S. cost compare globally?
rows.standfirst: U.S. stamps just had their sixth price hike since 2021. In raw numbers, only four countries in a recent study of 31 developed nations had cheaper stamps than the U.S.

rows.title: Ford expands a recall of thousands of its Bronco and Escape editions
rows.standfirst: Nearly 43,000 vehicles are impacted by the recall, including the 2022 Escape and the 2022 and 2023 Bronco Sport editions that have 1.5L engines.

rows.title: The IRS wants to do your taxes for free. Will it last?
rows.standfirst: With tax season upon us, many people are paying someone or a software to get their tax returns done. A small group of people, however, are filing online directly with ... the IRS. For free. Today on the show: how the IRS's tax filing experiment came to be, how it's been working so far, and who doesn't like it.

rows.title: The VA has its fix for a home loan debacle, but many vets who got hurt won't get help
rows.standfirst: The VA halted foreclosures after an NPR investigation found thousands of vets were facing foreclosure and it wasn't their fault. Now the VA's unveiling a rescue plan that leaves some out in the cold.

rows.title: White-sounding names get called back for jobs more than Black ones, a new study finds
rows.standfirst: Economists sent 83,000 fake job applications to a slew of major U.S. companies, and found that the typical firm favored white applicants over Black ones by around 9%.

rows.title: Five things to know as the tax deadline looms
rows.standfirst: April 15th, the deadline to file your income taxes, is just around the corner. Filings so far this year are on track with last year's, while the average refund is slightly larger.

rows.title: 4 negotiation tactics to try in everyday life
rows.standfirst: People often use negotiation tactics in business environments. But you can also use them to get your roommate to clean up, figure out where to eat for dinner or decide on which car to buy.

rows.title: Why the EU is investigating China's wind turbines
rows.standfirst: Europe wants clean energy, but it's struggling to compete with the low cost of China's green technology. The E.U. just announced it's investigating the subsidies received by Chinese wind turbine suppliers, which play a part in those low costs.

rows.title: How anti-diet culture got co-opted by big food brands
rows.standfirst: In recent years, the body positivity movement has raised its profile, especially on social media, largely through self-described anti-diet and body positivity influencers.

rows.title: How much does this cow weigh? (Classic)
rows.standfirst: This episode originally ran in 2015.

rows.title: Consumer Reports asks USDA to remove Lunchables from schools' lunch menus
rows.standfirst: The group found high levels of sodium and the presence of heavy metals in meal kits it tested. A Kraft Heinz spokesperson said all of its products meet strict safety standards.

rows.title: 6 months into war, Palestinians face high unemployment and a 'disastrous' economy
rows.standfirst: A Palestinian Authority official says there are around 700,000 Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza who have gone six months without work since the war between Israel and Hamas began on Oct. 7.

rows.title: Tesla cuts its car prices around the world after week of turmoil for the company
rows.standfirst: The company dropped its starting prices of its Model X, Model Y and Model S by $2,000 in the U.S.

rows.title: Startups want to cool Earth by reflecting sunlight. There are few rules and big risks
rows.standfirst: In a parking lot and on San Francisco Bay, NPR witnesses two different tests for solar geoengineering to tackle climate change. With much science unsettled, experts say regulations aren't keeping up.

rows.title: House approves sell-or-be-banned TikTok measure, attaching it to foreign aid bill
rows.standfirst: The bill, now advancing to the Senate, represents the most serious threat yet to the video app used by half of Americans.

rows.title: Biden administration restricts oil and gas leasing in Alaska's petroleum reserve
rows.standfirst: The administration said it will restrict new oil and gas leasing on 13 million acres in Alaska to help protect wildlife such as caribou and polar bears as the Arctic continues to warm.

rows.title: Volkswagen workers vote yes to unionizing, igniting UAW's push to organize the South
rows.standfirst: Volkswagen workers in Chattanooga, Tenn., voted overwhelmingly to unionize with the UAW, setting a new trajectory for labor unions in the American South.

rows.title: Ticketmaster's dominance, Caitlin Clark's paycheck, and other indicators
rows.standfirst: It's highs and lows in this edition of Indicators of the Week! The surprisingly high amount of electricity needed for artificial intelligence, basketball star Caitlin Clark's surprisingly low base salary, plus a potential crackdown on the ticketing company everyone loves to hate (possibly because of those high fees).

rows.title: FTX and the Serengeti of bankruptcy
rows.standfirst: For the last year and a half, the story of FTX has focused largely on the crimes and punishment of Sam Bankman-Fried. But in the background, the actual customers he left behind have been caught in a financial feeding frenzy over the remains of the company.

rows.title: Tesla recalls Cybertruck over sticky problem. Blame it on — yes — soap
rows.standfirst: Accelerator pedals on the new Cybertrucks can get stuck, a potentially dangerous production flaw. The reason why they're so sticky is soap.

rows.title: Which scientists get mentioned in the news? Mostly ones with Anglo names, says study
rows.standfirst: A new study finds that in news stories about scientific research, U.S. media were less likely to mention a scientist if they had an East Asian or African name, as compared to one with an Anglo name.

rows.title: Google worker says the company is 'silencing our voices' after dozens are fired
rows.standfirst: The tech giant fired 28 employees who took part in a protest over the company's Project Nimbus contract with the Israeli government. One fired worker tells her story.

rows.title: Inside the epic fight over new banking regulations
rows.standfirst: After the financial crisis of 2008, regulators around the world agreed banks should have more of a cushion to weather hard times. Now, U.S. regulators are once again looking to update minimum capital requirements through a set of proposals called Basel III Endgame. Today, on the show, a blow-by-blow account of this battle between bankers and regulators.

rows.title: Trump Media shares surge after a miserable run. Pros say stay away
rows.standfirst: Trump Media shares surged over the most recent two trading days — but the company continues to weather a miserable run since its stock market debut last month.

rows.title: Trader Joe's recalls basil linked to 12 salmonella infections in 7 states
rows.standfirst: The Food and Drug Administration warns Trader Joe's customers in dozens of states to throw out fresh basil after a federal investigation linked the product to a salmonella outbreak.

rows.title: 'S' is for solidarity, not strike. 'Sesame Street' writers reach a deal
rows.standfirst: The deal offers writers minimums for animation and new media programs, paid parental leave, protections against artificial intelligence and new media residuals.

rows.title: Housing costs keep inflation stubborn; New report on Maui wildfires released
rows.standfirst: Inflation is proving stubborn this year, and the cost of rent may be to blame. Hawaii's attorney general has released the first report into last year's Maui fires.

rows.title: Is the federal debt REALLY that bad?
rows.standfirst: Sandwiched between a burger joint and an oyster bar in New York City hangs a daunting image: The National Debt Clock. And that debt number? It just keeps ticking up. How deep in the hole are we? Nearly a hundred percent of gross domestic product. And counting. Today on the show, the federal debt. Is it time to freak out? Or is there nothing to see here?

rows.title: Fox News pulls down series as Hunter Biden threatens lawsuit
rows.standfirst: Fox News has taken down a six-part series in which it staged a mock trial of hypothetical criminal charges against Hunter Biden after the president's son threatened to sue the network.

rows.title: With a deadline looming, countries race for a global agreement to cut plastic waste
rows.standfirst: A United Nations official said negotiators have a "clear path to landing an ambitious deal" on plastic pollution. But environmentalists say the plastic industry is undermining an effective agreement.

rows.title: Top companies are on students' divest list. But does it really work?
rows.standfirst: Campus protesters want administrators to sell off investments in companies with ties to Israel. Here's a look at what divestment means — and why universities are saying no.

rows.title: Eight newspapers sue OpenAI, Microsoft for copyright infringement
rows.standfirst: The New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune and others contend that the tech companies illegally copied their work without seeking permission or ever paying the publishers.

rows.title: Wages, employment, inflation are up, causing headaches for the Fed
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady this week — and possibly for months to come — as policymakers try to sort through mixed signals about the U.S. economy.

rows.title: How do you counter misinformation? Critical thinking is step one
rows.standfirst: An economic perspective on misinformation

rows.title: U.S. to require automatic emergency braking on new vehicles in 5 years
rows.standfirst: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration unveiled the final version of the new regulation on Monday and called it the most significant safety rule in the past two decades.

rows.title: What consumers should know as Philips agrees to $1.1 billion CPAP settlement
rows.standfirst: Under a related deal, users who return devices by Aug. 9 can get an extra $100. As part of the recall, the company is offering repairs, replacements or refunds of the machines' cost.

rows.title: Taxing the final frontier
rows.standfirst: Launches by commercial space companies are becoming more frequent. Last year, the Federal Aviation Administration licensed 117, an all-time high. But these spaceflight companies aren't paying for all of the FAA's services that they use.

rows.title: UAW strike at Daimler Truck averted at 11th hour
rows.standfirst: More than 7,000 Daimler Truck workers, most of them in North Carolina, had threatened to go on strike. The UAW says the workers will get raises of at least 25% plus cost of living allowances.

rows.title: The case of the stolen masks
rows.standfirst: About thirty years ago, Yagya Kumar Pradhan woke up to the news that the temple he and his clan used had been broken into. The temple had been ransacked. And someone had stolen two holy Bhairav masks. Yagya says they had been in his family for more than five hundred years – since the 16th century.

rows.title: Biden administration abandons plan to ban menthol cigarettes, citing 'feedback'
rows.standfirst: An anti-smoking advocate says the decision to leave menthol cigarettes on the market "prioritizes politics over lives, especially Black lives."

rows.title: Video Game Industry Week: The Final Level
rows.standfirst: We wrap up our series on the economics of the video game industry with a triple roundup. Today, how the new ban on noncompete contracts could affect the gaming industry, whether young men are slacking off work to play games and the ever-controversial world of loot boxes.

rows.title: Net neutrality is back: U.S. promises fast, safe and reliable internet for all
rows.standfirst: The U.S. will reinstate Obama-era regulations for internet service providers that promise fast, reliable and fair internet speeds for all consumers. What happened when those rules were taken away?
